issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may remand a case for a retrial under Order XLI Rule 23-A of the Code of Civil Procedure only after reversing the decree for cogent reasons and finding a retrial necessary.
An appellate court cannot remand a case merely because it considers the evidence on record insufficient or because a party failed to produce evidence.
When the evidence on record permits the appellate court to decide the case, it must determine the appeal under Order XLI Rule 24 rather than remand the case for a de novo trial.
